In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reactions to loss of limb and loss of spouse are similar in many respects but that the reactions to the loss of spouse are more intense and more variable in nature.
the grief reaction to loss of limb was similar in form to that to loss of spouse, but that the intensity of the grief reaction to limb loss was less and that the grief reaction was more persistent.
the reactions of amputees and widows are similar in the early post loss phase, but in the amputees there is a more rapid and more complete resolution of the grief.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the grief reaction was more severe in the widows, but that the amputees had more difficulty in adapting to their loss.
the reactions of widows and amputees to loss are qualitatively very similar but quantitatively different, with widows showing greater distress in the early stages.
the reactions reported by the widows and the amputees were similar in many respects but that the reactions of the widows were more overt and more transient than the reactions of the amputees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of a limb or the loss of a spouse is not the same thing.
the loss of a limb, like the loss of a spouse, is associated with a period of grief, and that the grief associated with limb loss may be prolonged.
the psychological response to the loss of a loved one and the loss of a body part are very similar.
